title: OptiPIM: Optimizing Processing-in-Memory Acceleration Using Integer Linear Programming
problem: Efficient PIM acceleration requires precise software-hardware mapping that transforms application algorithms into PIM operations and data layouts, but existing PIM accelerators rely on manually tuned heuristics or exhaustive search, producing under-optimized mappings and/or prohibitively long optimization times.
motivation: PIM accelerators offer superior performance and energy efficiency by exploiting internal memory bandwidth, but realizing their potential requires automated, optimal mapping generation — a problem that manual heuristics fail to solve at scale.
method: OptiPIM reformulates the challenge of mapping operations to PIM hardware and arranging data—choosing where each computation should run and how data should be laid out—as an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) problem, a mathematical technique for finding the optimal solution when you have many constraints to satisfy. It builds accurate cost models (predictions of runtime efficiency for different choices) that efficiently represent the full design space. Implemented as a compiler pass within MLIR (an open-source framework that transforms high-level code like PyTorch into efficient hardware instructions), OptiPIM exploits the problem's structure to compute optimal mappings for PIM accelerators in just 4 minutes.
key_novelty: OptiPIM approaches PIM mapping using Integer Linear Programming (a mathematical method that finds the best solution to complex problems with many constraints) integrated into MLIR, automatically producing the mathematically optimal way to map data-intensive applications onto PIM accelerators in just 4 minutes.
contributions: PIM-friendly mapping representation with accurate cost modeling that defines a concise ILP formulation of the full design space
ILP-based optimization framework that generates optimal PIM mappings within 4 minutes
Integration into MLIR to support PyTorch workloads on PIM accelerators
Demonstrated at least 1.9x speedup over heuristic mappings on state-of-the-art PIM accelerators
baselines: manually tuned heuristics on state-of-the-art PIM accelerators
limitations: ILP tractability may degrade for very large design spaces beyond the workloads evaluated; generalization to non-ML data-intensive applications not fully demonstrated.
primary_theme: ILP-based optimal mapping for PIM accelerators
